newsitem.title: USA: Florida takes over insolvent insurance fund.
newsitem.headline: Florida takes over insolvent insurance fund.

text.p: Florida insurance regulators said Thursday they had taken over a failed workers' compensation self-insurance fund after the company reported losses for the year of $7.4 million.

Florida Employers Safety Association Self-Insurers Fund, which provided coverage for about 3,400 employers, was taken over late Tuesday after the state insurance department received a court order authorizing the transfer.
Financial statements obtained in August showed a $7.4 million deficit for the company, which let all its policies expire March 31, officials said.

The state is seeking $3.5 million from Fort Lauderdale-based Gulf Atlantic Management Co, which administered the FESA fund and received the money as payment for its services. State insurance officials, in their takeover petition filed in September, argue that the money should have been used to pay claims.

The vast majority of FESA's policies have been picked up by other insurers, but 1,500 claims remain the responsibility of FESA, including about 400 claims that pre-date the creation of a state safety net established in 1994 to pay claims in the event of an insolvency, officials said.

"The first thing we're going to do is take steps to begin getting policyholders' claims paid," Florida Insurance Commissioner Bill Nelson said Thursday in a statement. "Simultaneously, we'll be investigating why the company went broke and where all the money went."

Investigators Wednesday began a review of the books, said Dan McLaughlin, insurance department spokesman, adding that an issue of major concern was the payment of $3.5 million in management fees when it appeared that the fund had financial difficulties.

"We're not suggesting impropriety at this point," McLaughlin said. "We're questioning whether it was appropriate to pay all that money out at that time and whether or not they knew they'd be looking at some deficits."
